Lactate step tests from different sports, athletes and scenarios

Source: R/data.R
lactate_tests.Rd

Sixteen incremental step tests in long format, one row per stage, to try every part of lactater on real data: cycling, running, rowing and swimming; elite, trained and untrained athletes; one athlete tested six times over five years; and the cases that need care (an early lactate dip, no resting sample, 5-min steps, a submaximal test). Analyze one test with subset(), or several tests of one sport with .by = test.

Usage

lactate_tests

Format

A tibble with one row per stage and 13 columns:

test

the test: cycling_elite, cycling_female, cycling_early_dip, cycling_series_1 to cycling_series_6, running, rowing, cycling_5min_no_rest, swimming, untrained, submaximal, running_recreational.

athlete

the athlete; the six cycling_series tests share cyclist_series.

sport

cycling, running, rowing, or swimming, as in lactate_threshold(sport = ).

sex

M or F.

body_mass

body mass (kg) on the test day, NA when not reported.

day

days since the athlete's first test (0 for single tests).

description

who was tested, and how.

source

Trinity College Dublin (CC BY 4.0), Heuberger et al. 2018 (CC BY 4.0), or simulated.

step

the stage, 0 for the resting sample.

intensity

power (W) for cycling and rowing, speed (km/h) for running, speed (m/s) for swimming; 0 for the resting sample.

lactate

blood lactate (mmol/L).

heart_rate

heart rate (bpm), NA when not recorded.

rpe

rating of perceived exertion (Borg 6-20), simulated tests only; NA for the real tests.

Source

Trinity College Dublin graded exercise test data. Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.10841412 . License CC BY 4.0.

Heuberger JAAC, Gal P, Stuurman FE, de Muinck Keizer WAS, Mejia Miranda Y, Cohen AF. Repeatability and predictive value of lactate threshold concepts in endurance sports. PLOS ONE. 2018;13(11):e0206846. Data: figshare, doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.7240571 . License CC BY 4.0.

Details

Twelve tests are real: eleven from the Trinity College Dublin graded exercise test data (3-min stages, lactate sampled at 2 min, YSI analyzer; running on a treadmill at 0% grade; rowing with 1 min of rest between stages) and one from Heuberger et al. (2018) (5-min steps from 175 W). Names, birth dates and test dates were removed. Four tests are simulated, where no open data exists: a swimmer's 7 x 200 m step test (+0.05 m/s per step; Pelarigo et al., 2017), an untrained client tested to exhaustion and stopped early (25 W steps; untrained men peaked near 250 W in Messonnier et al., 2013), and a recreational runner on the protocol of Roecker et al. (1998) (treadmill at 2% grade, +2 km/h every 3 min from 6 km/h), so that their race-time equations apply as published. Their lactate rises exponentially through about 2.5 mmol/L near the first threshold, with analyzer scatter of 3% from 2 mmol/L and 5% below (Bonaventura et al., 2015). Their simulated RPE rises with lactate, from about 11 at 2 mmol/L to 14 at 4 mmol/L (close to the cohort means at the first rise in lactate and at 4 mmol/L of Scherr et al., 2013) and 19 to 20 at the last stage. See data-raw/lactate_tests.R.

References

Bonaventura JM, Sharpe K, Knight E, Fuller KL, Tanner RK, Gore CJ. Reliability and accuracy of six hand-held blood lactate analysers. Journal of Sports Science and Medicine. 2015;14:203-214.

Messonnier LA, Emhoff CAW, Fattor JA, Horning MA, Carlson TJ, Brooks GA. Lactate kinetics at the lactate threshold in trained and untrained men. Journal of Applied Physiology. 2013;114(11):1593-1602.

Pelarigo JG, Machado L, Fernandes RJ, Greco CC, Vilas-Boas JP. Oxygen uptake kinetics and energy system's contribution around maximal lactate steady state swimming intensity. PLOS ONE. 2017;12(2):e0167263.

Roecker K, Schotte O, Niess AM, Horstmann T, Dickhuth HH. Predicting competition performance in long-distance running by means of a treadmill test. Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise. 1998;30(10):1552-1557.

Scherr J, Wolfarth B, Christle JW, Pressler A, Wagenpfeil S, Halle M. Associations between Borg's rating of perceived exertion and physiological measures of exercise intensity. European Journal of Applied Physiology. 2013;113(1):147-155.
